Pitfalls and Error Names

Table 29. Servlet pitfalls, their symptoms and fixes (rows marked "observed" were reproduced on Tomcat 11.0.26)
Symptom or error Cause Fix

Counters or user data mix between users

Per-request data in servlet or filter fields: one instance serves all threads

Keep state in local variables, request, session or thread-safe application objects; make fields immutable or atomic

getParameter returns null for a form field

The body was read first with getReader() or getInputStream()

Read parameters first, or wrap the request and serve the cached body

Ã± instead of ñ (observed)

Request charset undefined, container default ISO-8859-1, or setCharacterEncoding called after the first parameter read

<request-character-encoding>UTF-8, or set it first in a filter; <response-character-encoding>

Header or status change has no effect (observed)

The response was already committed by a flush, a full buffer or a forward

Set headers before writing; use resetBuffer/reset only before commit

IllegalStateException from sendError, sendRedirect, forward, getSession, reset (observed)

The response is committed

Create the session and decide errors before writing; return after sendError or sendRedirect

IllegalStateException from getWriter or getOutputStream

A servlet or JSP mixed the writer and the stream

Use one; set the type before the first call

Empty page with Content-Length: 0 after a response-wrapping filter (observed)

The filter was mapped to REQUEST, but a forward closes the real response before the filter’s post-processing runs

Map the filter to the forwarded resource with <dispatcher>FORWARD</dispatcher>

A filter does not run on a forward, include or error page (observed)

A mapping without <dispatcher> is REQUEST only

List FORWARD, INCLUDE, ERROR, ASYNC explicitly

Filters run in a surprising order

Annotations give no order; <servlet-name> mappings run after all <url-pattern> mappings (observed)

Declare order-sensitive filters in web.xml

The request is silently blocked

A filter forgot chain.doFilter, or continued after sendError

Return after blocking; call the chain exactly once

getRequestURI() shows the wrong path inside an included page (observed)

Path methods describe the including request

Read the jakarta.servlet.include.* attributes

IllegalStateException from startAsync

A filter or servlet in the path is not async-capable

Set asyncSupported=true on all of them

Redirect lands on the wrong host behind a proxy

Relative or context-relative Location (Tomcat 11 default) behind a path-rewriting proxy

Set useRelativeRedirects on the context, or fix the proxy

Refresh re-posts the form

The response to a POST was a 200 page

Answer with 303 and a GET (Post/Redirect/Get)

Session id in URLs and logs (observed)

URL rewriting is on until the cookie is confirmed

<tracking-mode>COOKIE</tracking-mode>

Session fixation

The session id was not rotated at login (observed rotation)

request.changeSessionId() on login and privilege change

Cookie missing in the next request

Wrong path or domain, Secure over HTTP, SameSite blocking a cross-site request, a size or count limit

Check the Set-Cookie line against the request URL; cookies carry only name and value back

getCookies() is null

The request had no cookie header

Test for null first

Cookie value built from request data

Header injection and tampering

Validate against an allowlist, keep the value opaque

ClassNotFoundException: javax.servlet... on Tomcat 10 and 11, or "Invalid <url-pattern>" at deployment (observed)

javax.* code needs migration, or a pattern mixes wildcards

Rename to jakarta.* or run the Tomcat migration tool; use only exact, prefix, extension, / and "" patterns

404 for a view under WEB-INF (observed)

Container refuses direct access to WEB-INF

Forward to it from a controller; this is the desired behaviour

JSP page shown without data

A browser requested the view directly instead of the controller

Keep views under WEB-INF and map controllers

Error page shows the wrong exception or none (observed)

java.lang.Throwable declared as <exception-type> hides the root-cause pass; the default entry gets exception but not exception_type

Use the default entry as catch-all; read jakarta.servlet.error.exception

Truncated response, curl: (18) (observed)

An exception after the response was committed cannot reach an error page

Do risky work before the first flush

Upload accepts huge files, or a non-multipart POST gives 500 (observed)

Limits left unlimited by default; no content-type check

Set maxFileSize and maxRequestSize, check Content-Type, answer 413 and 415

Files overwritten or written outside the upload folder

The client’s file name was used as a path

Generate the file name on the server; use getSubmittedFileName only for display

NotSerializableException or IllegalArgumentException on session replication

A non-serializable object in a session of a distributable application

Store Serializable values only, and keep sessions small

Memory growth under load

Large objects in sessions and long idle timeouts

Store ids, not graphs; shorten the timeout; invalidate on logout

Thread starvation

Blocking calls in the request thread under high concurrency

Use startAsync for slow remote calls, or measure virtual threads

Source: Jakarta Servlet 6.1 — Appendix A, Change Log

What Changed Recently

Table 30. Servlet 6.1 (Jakarta EE 11)
Change Detail

Redirect control

sendRedirect overloads with status and clearBuffer; containers may send relative Location headers (issues 74, 275)

Error dispatch

jakarta.servlet.error.query_string, and jakarta.servlet.error.method; error dispatches are always GET (issues 59, 544)

HttpSession.Accessor

getAccessor() lets applications (typically WebSocket) work with a session outside a request (issue 546)

Cookies

Valueless attributes (HttpOnly, Secure, Partitioned) clarified (issue 571)

Parameters

Parameter methods may throw a runtime exception when parsing fails (issue 431); ServletContext path methods carry a security note and canonicalization rules (issue 453)

API additions

Charset overloads of setCharacterEncoding, ByteBuffer support on ServletInputStream/ServletOutputStream, constants 308, 421, 422, 426, secure_protocol request attribute

HTTP/2 server push

Deprecated and optional (issue 538)

Spec hygiene

SecurityManager references removed; TRACE responses drop sensitive headers; HTTPS support clarified; CONNECT requests are rejected by default

Next

Servlet 6.2 is in progress (milestone 6.2.0-M2 on Maven Central); it is part of the Jakarta EE 12 work and is not required for anything on this page
Table 31. Servlet 6.0 (Jakarta EE 10)
Change Detail

Removals

SingleThreadModel, HttpSessionContext, HttpUtils, and the deprecated methods that went with them (for example encodeUrl, encodeRedirectUrl, HttpServletRequest.isRequestedSessionIdFromUrl, ServletContext.getServlet, HttpSession.getValue, putValue)

Cookies

RFC 6265 replaces RFC 2109; generic cookie attributes with setAttribute/getAttribute (so SameSite); setComment and setVersion deprecated for removal

HTTP methods

PATCH supported (doPatch); doHead no longer wraps the response, container-implemented HEAD

Identifiers

getRequestId, getProtocolRequestId, getServletConnection

Descriptor

<cookie-config><attribute> configures extra session-cookie attributes such as SameSite

Platform

Java 11 minimum; module-info; X-Powered-By recommendation dropped
Table 32. Servlet 5.0 and the namespace
Change Detail

javax.servlet to jakarta.servlet

The only change of 5.0 (Jakarta EE 9); a Servlet 4.0 application becomes 5.0 and later by renaming packages (spec Appendix A.3)

Tomcat

10.0 implemented 5.0 and is end of life; 10.1 implements 6.0; 11 implements 6.1. The Tomcat migration tool converts javax WARs automatically

Source: Jakarta Servlet 6.1 — A.1 Changes Since Jakarta Servlet 6.0

Source: Jakarta Servlet 6.1 — A.2 Changes Since Jakarta Servlet 5.0

Source: Jakarta Servlet 6.1 — A.3 Compatibility with Jakarta Servlet Specification Version 4.0

Source: Apache Tomcat — Migration Guide to Tomcat 10

Source: Apache Tomcat — Migration Tool for Jakarta EE

Where the Books Are Outdated

Web Development with JavaServer Pages (Manning, 2001, listed in the section bibliography) is written for the Servlet 2.3 API and Tomcat 4. The concepts it covers on this page survived unchanged: lifecycle, request and response, sessions, filters, listeners and the WAR layout. The details have not.

Table 33. Servlet 2.3-era material and its modern equivalent
The book’s era Today (Servlet 6.1)

javax.servlet.* packages

jakarta.servlet.* since Jakarta EE 9; Tomcat 10 and later do not run the old names

SingleThreadModel to make a servlet safe

Removed in 6.0; make the servlet stateless or thread-safe

HttpUtils.getRequestURL, HttpSessionContext, session.getValue/putValue, response.encodeUrl

Removed in 6.0; use request.getRequestURL(), getAttribute/setAttribute, encodeURL

web.xml with a <!DOCTYPE web-app PUBLIC "-//Sun Microsystems..."> DTD

The web-app_6_1.xsd schema and version="6.1"; most elements are optional because annotations exist

Every servlet, filter and listener declared in web.xml

@WebServlet, @WebFilter, @WebListener, @MultipartConfig; web.xml only for ordering and overrides

<taglib> directly under <web-app>

<jsp-config>, or automatic TLD discovery in JARs

ISO-8859-1 assumed, request.setCharacterEncoding in every servlet

<request-character-encoding> and <response-character-encoding>; UTF-8 everywhere

Cookie attributes limited to those of RFC 2109 (setComment, setVersion)

RFC 6265 and Cookie.setAttribute for SameSite and Partitioned; setComment and setVersion are deprecated for removal

Session id in the URL as a normal fallback

Cookies only; URL rewriting leaks the id

Application-managed login with a session attribute and a role filter

Container-managed or framework authentication; if you keep an application login, call changeSessionId() at login

File upload with a third-party multipart library

@MultipartConfig and Part, built in since Servlet 3.0

No asynchronous processing, no non-blocking I/O

startAsync, ReadListener, WriteListener, and (6.1) ByteBuffer streams

Servlet and listener ordering by tool convention

<absolute-ordering>, <ordering> in fragments, <load-on-startup>

HttpSessionActivationListener and bindings as the only session hooks

Same interfaces, plus HttpSessionIdListener (3.1) and HttpSession.Accessor (6.1)

jsp:plugin and applets for rich clients

Removed from Pages 4.0; applets no longer run in browsers

Tomcat 4 directories and server.xml contexts

Tomcat 11 with webapps/, conf/Catalina/localhost/*.xml and context.xml; CATALINA_BASE separation

Source: Jakarta Servlet 6.1 — A.4 Changes Since Jakarta Servlet 4.0

Source: Manning — Web Development with JavaServer Pages, Second Edition
